column1: # Which applied migration is documented by which file.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# db/ is documentation of what was applied, and it had drifted badly: 65
# migrations were applied to the live project and 39 files described them. Two
# whole features - account deletion and content moderation - existed only in
# production. A P0 fix (security_invoker on matches_public) was silently undone
# by a later migration and nothing noticed for eight days.
# The live migration NAME and the repo FILENAME do not match each other, and
# should not have to: one is a Supabase identifier, the other is a date-ordered
# document. So the mapping is written down rather than guessed at, and
# scripts/verify-schema-documented.mjs fails when a version applied to the
# project is missing from this list.
# Columns are tab-separated: version, name, file.
# The file column takes one of three values:
#   db/migrations/<name>.sql   the file documenting it
#   PRE-DB                     applied before db/ existed. db/README.md is
#                              explicit that this directory is a partial
#                              history, not a baseline - these are the part it
#                              never covered, and backfilling them means
#                              dumping the schema, which is a different job
#                              (see db/README.md's last paragraph).
#   FOLDED:<file>              applied as its own migration, documented inside
#                              a file that covers the whole change.
# ADDING A MIGRATION: write the file, apply it, add its row here. All three, or
# the check fails - which is the point.
